claim: The benchmark studies whether a system retrieves relevant evidence, selects the correct temporal version, integrates distributed information, and produces an answer supported by verifiable citations.
Every bilingual pair represents the same semantic content while using natural wording in each language.
Conceptual identifiers, relations, and inclusion decisions must be equivalent across both versions.
The benchmark distinguishes direct, temporal, multi-hop, version-comparison, and unanswerable questions.
An unanswerable question must genuinely lack sufficient evidence; a retrieval failure does not turn an answerable question into an unanswerable one.
The first official version contains 2,302 semantic questions and 4,604 language records.
Every semantic question has one Spanish and one English version.
The benchmark does not require one exact wording, but every important claim must be covered by evidence.
Every question records its intent, difficulty, answer, required facts, sources, citations, and reference date.
The annotator must justify why the category is appropriate and state discarded alternatives.
ES/EN pairs share category, evidence, and decision even where wording is naturally adapted.
Review checks that the question does not depend on external knowledge or an interpretation unsupported by the corpus.

evidence: Probability, impact, control, owner, and evidence are recorded.
Mitigation includes automated checks, manual review, and regression tests.
If the risk materializes, publication of the affected result stops and experiments requiring repetition are identified.
The risk closes only where the correction is reproducible and the report clearly distinguishes valid and archived results.
